<STRUCT_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces which is
fppf local on the target and preserved by arbitrary base change.
Let <MATH_0002> be a morphism of algebraic stacks
representable by algebraic spaces. Then we say
<TEXTITOPEN_0001><MATH_0003> has property <MATH_0004><TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if and only if for every scheme <MATH_0005>
and morphism <MATH_0006> the morphism of algebraic spaces
<MATH_0007> has property <MATH_0008>, see
Algebraic Stacks,
Definition <REF_0001>.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
It turns out that if <MATH_0009> is representable
by algebraic spaces and has property <MATH_0010>, then for any morphism of algebraic
stacks <MATH_0011> the base change
<MATH_0012>
has property <MATH_0013>, see
Algebraic Stacks,
Lemmas <REF_0002> and
<REF_0003>.
If the property <MATH_0014> is preserved under compositions, then this holds
also in the setting of morphisms of algebraic stacks representable by
algebraic spaces, see
Algebraic Stacks,
Lemmas <REF_0004> and
<REF_0005>.
Moreover, in this case products
<MATH_0015>
of morphisms representable by algebraic spaces having property <MATH_0016>
have property <MATH_0017>, see
Algebraic Stacks, Lemma
<REF_0006>.

<STRUCT_0004><STRUCT_0005>
Finally, if we have two properties <MATH_0018> of morphisms of algebraic spaces
which are fppf local on the target and preserved by arbitrary base change
and if <MATH_0019> for every morphism <MATH_0020>, then the same
implication holds for the corresponding property of morphisms of algebraic
stacks representable by algebraic spaces, see
Algebraic Stacks, Lemma
<REF_0007>.
We will use this <TEXTITOPEN_0002>without further mention<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> in the following and in the
following chapters.
